title: The Address of Life Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A letter crosses India and lands at one single house, because each line of the address narrows the search. Aarav asks: does every living thing have an address like this? It does.

You will see what a rank, a taxonomic category, the taxonomic hierarchy and a taxon are. Wheat walks down its address in a live zoom through nested groups (Plantae, Angiospermae, Monocotyledonae, Poales, Poaceae, Triticum, aestivum), then climbs back up while the number of members grows and the shared features fall. We build the rule step by step, see insects, mammals and dogs as taxa, compare phylum (animals) with division (plants), and in the worked example find where wheat and mango part ways. Then the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions.

This is Episode 6 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 An address for every living thing
0:27 Rank, category, hierarchy and taxon
0:47 Wheat walks down its address
1:18 Climbing back up: members vs shared features
1:38 The rule, step by step
2:04 Taxa at different levels + pause and think
2:44 Phylum vs division
3:00 Worked example: wheat and mango
3:24 Exam trap: kingdom vs genus
3:46 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:10 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Species, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum and Kingdom. Mango, potato, housefly and human: what does each rank really mean?
